'''Wubbo Johannes Ockels''' (28 March 1946&nbsp;– 18 May 2014) was a Dutch [[physicist]] and [[astronaut]] with the [[European Space Agency]] who, in 1985, became the first Dutch citizen in space when he flew on [[STS-61-A]] as a [[payload specialist]]. He later became professor of [[aerospace engineering]] at [[Delft University of Technology]].

==Education and early life==
Ockels was born in [[Almelo]], [[Netherlands]], but considered [[Groningen]] to be his hometown. He obtained his [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] in 1973 and subsequently a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in the same subjects in 1978 from the [[University of Groningen]]. His thesis was based on experimental work at the Nuclear-physics Accelerator Institute (KVI) in Groningen.

From 1973 to 1978, Ockels performed experimental investigations at the Nuclear Physics Accelerator Institute in Groningen. His work concerned the [[Gamma ray|gamma-ray]] [[Radioactive decay|decay]] of nuclear systems directly after formation and the development of a data-handling system involving design of electronics and programming of [[Real-time computing|real-time software]]. He also contributed to the design and construction of position-sensitive charged particle detectors. While at the K.V.I. Institute, Ockels supervised the practical work of first-year physics students at the University of Groningen.

==ESA career==
[[File:Wubbo Ockels.jpg|thumb|Wubbo Ockels as an astronaut]]
[[File:STS-61-A crew.jpg|thumb|The [[STS-61-A]] crew with Ockels second from the right]]
[[File:Wubbo-sl1.jpg|thumb|Ockels in [[Spacelab]]]]
In 1978, Ockels was selected by the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) as one of three European [[payload specialist]]s to train for the [[STS-9|Spacelab 1]] mission. In May 1980, under the terms of an agreement between ESA and [[NASA]], Ockels and Swiss astronaut [[Claude Nicollier]] were selected to begin basic mission specialist training with the NASA astronaut candidates at NASA's [[Johnson Space Center]], [[Houston, Texas]].

In September 1981 Ockels withdrew from training to focus on Spacelab, and did not become a NASA mission specialist.<ref name="cfu2019">{{Cite book |last1=Croft |first1=Melvin |title=Come Fly with Us: NASA's Payload Specialist Program |last2=Youskauskas |first2=John |publisher=University of Nebraska Press |year=2019 |pages=63–64 |isbn=9781496212252 |series=[[Outward Odyssey]]: a People's History of Spaceflight}}</ref> He rejoined the Spacelab 1 crew for training as a back-up payload specialist to operate experiments. This mission of a reusable, scientific research facility built by the European Space Agency (ESA) took place aboard the Space Shuttle in November 1983. Spacelab 1 was a joint NASA/ESA mission. He was the first Dutch citizen astronaut, not the first Dutch-born astronaut, as he is preceded by the naturalized American [[Lodewijk van den Berg]], who flew on [[STS-51-B]]. Having served his role as back-up payload specialist for German astronaut [[Ulf Merbold]], he took his place in Mission Control in Houston as the primary communicator between the astronauts working in Spacelab and the Mission Management Team in Houston.

Ockels flew as a payload specialist on the crew of [[STS-61-A|STS-61A Challenger]] (30 October to 6 November 1985). [[STS-61-A|STS-61A]] was the West German D-1 Spacelab mission. It was the first to carry eight crew members, (five Americans, two Germans and Ockels); the largest to fly in space; and was also the first in which payload activities were controlled from outside the United States: from the DLR control center in Germany. More than 75 scientific experiments were completed in the areas of [[physiology|physiological sciences]], [[materials science]], [[biology]], and [[navigation]]. At mission conclusion Ockels had traveled 2.5 million miles in 110 Earth orbits, and logged over 168 hours in space.

Ockels was a member of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[European Physical Society]]. From 1999 to 2003, he was head of ESA's Office for Educational Projects Outreach Activities.

A [[minor planet]] was named after Wubbo Ockels by the [[International Astronomical Union]]. The asteroid orbits the Sun between [[Mars]] and [[Jupiter]]. The object's full name is [[List of minor planets: 9001–10000#496|9496 Ockels]].

==Scientific career==
In 1992, Ockels was appointed part-time professor of [[aerospace engineering]] (in particular, Aerospace for Sustainable Engineering and Technology) at Delft University of Technology, and promoted to full-time professor in September 2003. In this function, he oversaw the [[Nuna]] projects. He also proposed the development of a [[Superbus (transport)|Superbus]], a new method of high speed (250&nbsp;km/hour) [[public transport]]ation by road. The public transportation company [[Connexxion]] was the first company to invest in the development of this Superbus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tudelft.nl/live/pagina.jsp?id=30380163-f32c-4c33-a943-8512116edd8a&lang=nl|title=TU Delft - Connexxion steekt geld in Superbus<!-- Bot generated title -->}}</ref>

{{Blockquote | style=font-size:100%; | text=The LadderMill is the response to the challenge for exploiting the gigantic energy source contained in the airspace up to high altitudes of 10 km. The concept has been developed with the aim to convert wind energy at altitude in electricity on the ground in an environmental and cost effective manner.}}

While working at the university he assisted and advised the [[Nuna|Nuon Solar Team]], a [[Solar car racing|solar racer]] team consisting of students, which won the biennial [[World Solar Challenge]] four consecutive times from 2001 to 2007. Ockels was also the initiator of the [[Superbus (transport)|Superbus]] project. He also cofounded the sustainable engineering firm "The Green Canals" (De Groene Grachten).

In 2009, Ockels presented a talk arguing that the notion of [[Philosophy of space and time|time]] is human-constructed as a result of our interpretation of the effects of gravity.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tedxamsterdam.com/2009/video-wubbo-ockels-on-time-and-gravity/ |title=VIDEO: Wubbo Ockels on time and gravity « TEDxAmsterdam |website=www.tedxamsterdam.com |access-date=13 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100507183436/http://www.tedxamsterdam.com/2009/video-wubbo-ockels-on-time-and-gravity/ |archive-date=7 May 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ockels was married, had two children and two grandchildren.

His sister was politician [[Marjet Ockels]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/id/vk49garygxzc/nieuws/oud_pvda_dissidente_marjet_ockels |title=Oud-PvdA-dissidente Marjet Ockels overleden |language=nl |publisher=Parlement.com |date=19 May 2016 |access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref>

===Health and death===
In August 2005, Ockels suffered a severe [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]], which required his hospitalization. He recovered well and was able to resume his work at the [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.expatica.com/nl/articles/news/former-dutch-astronaut-improving-in-hospital-23114.html|title=News Former Dutch astronaut improving in hospital - News from the Netherlands - Expatica<!-- Bot generated title -->|date=25 August 2005}}</ref> On 29 May 2013 it was announced that Ockels had an aggressive form of [[kidney cancer]] ([[renal cell carcinoma]]) with a [[metastasis]] in his [[pleural cavity]], and a life expectancy of one to two years.<ref>{{in lang|nl}} [http://www.destentor.nl/2.2545/show/wubbo-ockels-heeft-agressieve-vorm-van-nierkanker-1.3841310 Wubbo Ockels heeft agressieve vorm van nierkanker], Destentor.nl, 29 May 2013</ref> He died from complications of cancer on 18 May 2014.<ref>{{in lang|nl}}[http://nos.nl/artikel/649348-wubbo-ockels-overleden.html Wubbo Ockels overleden], nos.nl, 18 May 2014</ref>

==Honours==
*Officer of the [[Order of Orange-Nassau]] (Netherlands)<ref name="KB">[http://resolver.kb.nl/resolve?urn=ddd:011011476:mpeg21:a0008 Lintje voor Wubbo Ockels] - Nieuwsblad van het Noorden (Dutch newspaper), 18-11-1985</ref>
*Merit Cross 1st Class (Officer's Cross) of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]<ref name="TUDelft">{{cite web | title=Zoeken | website=TU Delft | url=http://www.lr.tudelft.nl/en/current/latest-news/article/detail/in-memoriam-profdr-wubbo-ockels/ | language=nl | access-date=2020-08-24 | author1=Communication }}</ref>
* NASA Public Service Award<ref name="TUDelft"/>
* NASA Space Flight Medal<ref name="TUDelft"/>
* Generaal Snijdersfonds Gold Medal (the highest aviation award in the Netherlands)<ref name="TUDelft"/>

==In popular culture==
{{in popular culture|section|date=February 2025}}

* On March 28, 2020, [[Google]] celebrated his 74th birthday with a [[Google Doodle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://doodles.google/doodle/wubbo-ockels-74th-birthday/|title=Wubbo Ockels' 74th Birthday|website=Google|date=28 March 2020}}</ref>

* A fictional version of Ockels played by Norwegian actor Bjørn Alexander appears in the second season of the alternate history space drama show ''[[For All Mankind (TV series)|For All Mankind]]'', in which he crashes his rover on the Moon during a [[solar storm]] and is saved by a lead character, Molly.

* Wubbo Ockels Base is among the names that get assigned to space habitats in the 2022 grand strategy 4X game ''[[Terra Invicta]]''.

* Dutch rapper [[Donnie (Dutch rapper)|Donnie]] has released a song in 2015 called "Wubbo Ockels", produced by [[Bas Bron]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://3voor12.vpro.nl/artikelen/clipprimeur-de-master-eyeliner-game-van-donnie-in-wubbo-ockels|title=Clipprimeur: De master eyeliner game van Donnie in Wubbo Ockels|website=3voor12|date=24 November 2015|trans-title=Music video premiere: Donnie's master eyeliner game in Wubbo Ockels|language=Dutch|access-date=2 April 2026}}</ref>

* Indiepop band [[John Wayne Shot Me]] recorded a song called "Wubbo Ockels" for their album ''The Purple Hearted Youth Club''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://myspace.com/johnwayneshotme|title=john wayne shot me &#124; Listen and Stream Free Music, Albums, New Releases, Photos, Videos|website=Myspace}}</ref>

* Dutch cowpunk band Freaking Farmer Boys wrote a tribute to Wubbo Ockels: Wubbo oh Wubbo. They played the song during their live concerts in 1986 and 1987, and it has survived on some of their demo tapes.
